title: Partner Co-sell Pipeline Review - BriskBridge
summary: Quarterly co-sell pipeline review with BriskBridge. Covered top 3 deals, alignment on motions (who owns discovery vs. demo), open security questions (SOC 2 scope, SSO), and next steps to accelerate two hot deals via executive intro + joint benchmark. Agreed to run a short Dedicated vs Hosted TCO comparison for Acme Retail POC.
topics: POC timelines and next exec steps
next_steps: Maya to share joint deck and updated co-sell spreadsheet by 12/15
Jordan to schedule 2-hour technical benchmark with Acme Retail by 12/18
Alex to coordinate exec intro for Zenith Logistics by 12/20
action_items: Maya Patel: Share joint partner co-sell deck and pricing notes - due 2026-12-15
Jordan Lee: Set up Dedicated vs Hosted benchmark session and invite Acme Retail SEs - due 2026-12-18
Alex Kim: Arrange exec intro to Zenith Logistics VP of Product - due 2026-12-20
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-12
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Jordan Lee, Carlos Mendez (Redwood) / Alex Kim, Priya Rao, Tom Henderson (BriskBridge)

Summary: quick run through of co-sell pipeline; a few noisy lines from phone into recording so apologies for bits of bleed.

[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Alex (BriskBridge): Hi Maya, Alex here. Priya and Tom are on as well.
[00:00:12] Priya (BriskBridge): Hey all.
[00:00:15] Jordan (Redwood): Jordan here, will cover the tech bench items later.
[00:00:18] Tom (BriskBridge): Tom joined.
[00:00:21] Maya: Cool. Agenda — pipeline review, top three deals, any blockers, security asks, then wrap with owners & next steps.
[00:00:30] Alex: Sounds good. We'll start with Zenith Logistics — that's our largest joint opp right now.
[00:00:36] Priya: Quick context: Zenith is evaluating an internal routing assistant for their fleet ops, they have strict data residency needs — EU-only — and they want a POC by end of Q1.
[00:00:50] Jordan: For Zenith, we flagged two options — Hosted Redwood API vs Redwood Dedicated in their EU region. From perf numbers, Dedicated gives more predictable latency for spiky loads, but cost is higher. We can run a short benchmark to quantify.
[00:01:10] Alex: The buying committee is procurement + infra + lead product. Security will push on SOC 2 type 2 and KMS. Are we comfortable with how Redwood surfaces KMS integration details?
[00:01:22] Maya: Yes, we have an integration pattern doc — I'll share the link after the call. We also have SOC 2 attestation; Jordan, can you help surface the audit scope overlap for Dedicated/private?
[00:01:33] Jordan: Yep, I'll pull the SOC 2 matrix and mark the bits relevant to Dedicated and Private deployments.
[00:01:39] Tom: Also curious about audit logs — we need field-level tracing for some requests, is that in Redwood Console?
[00:01:46] Carlos (Redwood): Console has request-level traces, and we can surface token-level cost and latency. Field-level payloads are sensitive — we usually recommend pseudonymization before they hit logging.
[00:01:58] Alex: Ok thanks. Next deal: Acme Retail — mid-market chain, high volume of product search queries, they care about per-token cost.
[00:02:07] Priya: For Acme, the ask is a POC around reranking + embedding similarity. They want example latency under 150ms p95 for search reranks.
[00:02:18] Jordan: That p95 is doable on Dedicated with the right batching config and KV cache priming; on Hosted it might be tight during peak hour. We should propose a dedicated pool for the POC, then run a cost/perf side-by-side.
[00:02:33] Maya: Action: Jordan to schedule a two hour bench with Acme's SEs. We'll include Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization) in the runbook.
[00:02:44] Alex: Who owns the demo content? BriskBridge can own the sample dataset for search.
[00:02:50] Maya: Great, Alex and Priya to coordinate dataset handoff.
[00:02:55]
[00:03:05] Alex: Third one is Zenith partner? Wait we already did Zenith. There's also Zenith, Acme, and Zenith — haha — sorry, I mean Zenith, Acme, and Zenith had the largest ARR but there's also LumenWorks which is earlier stage.
[00:03:18] Jordan: For LumenWorks, it's more of an exploratory POC; they'll likely be fine with Hosted to start. We can propose a low-effort integration path.
[00:03:27] Priya: On the commercial front — how does crediting work between Redwood and BriskBridge for joint leads? We had some questions from our finance team.
[00:03:35] Maya: We can codify a co-sell crediting spreadsheet. Typically revenue crediting is 50/50 for joint sourced deals under 200k, but we can be flexible — I'll include a template and you can route to your finance.
[00:03:46] Tom: Good. Also procurement asked about terms: data residency, breach liability cap, and indemnity — any templated counsel we can share?
[00:03:55] Carlos: We have a legal playbook and sample terms sheet. I'll attach the security/legal pack.
[00:04:02] Alex: Perfect.
[00:04:10]
[00:04:45] [Speaker 1]: (mumble) — we had a question — is there a difference in SLAs between Dedicated and Private?
[00:04:52] Jordan: Yes — Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency and uptime per the contract; Private depends on the deployment model and infra you run — our support tiers cover that. For public Hosted, SLAs are lower but easier to start.
[00:05:06] Maya: A lot of customers start Hosted to iterate, then move to Dedicated once they need capacity predictability.
[00:05:12] Priya: For the EU residency ask, can Redwood do a VPC-based private deployment inside customer's cloud?
[00:05:19] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private can be deployed into a customer VPC or via our Private offering with region controls. There are ops prerequisites — network peering, KMS, and audit logging setup. We'll document the path.
[00:05:31] Alex: On the technical blockers — LLM model choice was raised in a couple of deals; some prefer open models for cost, others want model parity with Anthropic. Can we do model mapping for cost and latency?
[00:05:43] Jordan: We can produce a model mapping doc — show performance profiles (latency/cost/quality) for a few variants. Redwood Verify profiles are useful there.
[00:05:52] Maya: I'll include that in the deck.
[00:06:00]
[00:06:45] Tom: One ask from Zenith — they want a short executive briefing for their VP of Ops. Can we do a 30 minute exec call?
[00:06:53] Maya: Yes, we can do that. Alex, will you coordinate the invite?
[00:06:58] Alex: Yep I'll set up the intro.
[00:07:05]
[00:07:30] Jordan: Quick note on benchmarks — we'll test sequence length distribution, batch sizes, cold vs warm KV cache, and also quantify token cost delta for int8 quant vs fp16. That should help commercial conversation.
[00:07:45] Priya: For Acme's 150ms p95, what size instances are you thinking?
[00:07:51] Jordan: Likely A100-class or equivalent for low latency under heavy load; we'll model with both A10/30 and A100 to give cost options.
[00:07:59]
[00:08:30] Maya: Any blockers from BriskBridge side on the co-sell motion itself? E.g., enablement, deal registration, credits?
[00:08:38] Alex: We need a clear co-sell folder in your partner portal with up-to-date decks, an intro template, and a deal registration flow. Also, quick legal template would speed procurement.
[00:08:50] Carlos: We'll create a partner folder and share links; Maya will send the deck.
[00:08:56]
[00:09:40] Priya: A small thing — is there a recommended way to handle sensitive PII in conversation with Redwood for POCs? They need a procedure for sample masking.
[00:09:50] Jordan: We advise pseudonymization before sending into logs or persisted traces. For POCs we can use synthetic datasets. We'll add a runbook note.
[00:09:59]
[00:10:20] Alex: On timeline — Zenith wants POC kickoff in Jan; Acme wants POC in Feb. Are those realistic?
[00:10:26] Maya: Yes, Jan kickoff for Zenith is ok, we need to finalize requirements and exec intro this month. Acme in Feb is also fine, benchmark in Dec to confirm.
[00:10:36]
[00:11:10] Jordan: I'll follow up with a proposed benchmark plan and a runbook template.
[00:11:15] Maya: Great. Any risks we should call out?
[00:11:19] Tom: Risk: procurement cycles slipping into Q2, data residency legal review delays.
[00:11:24] Priya: Also risk on model quality — if we push a smaller quantized model and quality drops, it could hurt adoption. Need eval criteria up front.
[00:11:33] Maya: We'll include eval criteria and guardrails in the runbook.
[00:11:40]
[00:12:05] Alex: A quick commercial note — BriskBridge team requests a joint pricing worksheet for different POC flavours (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) so they can show internal cost backs.
[00:12:16] Maya: I'll put together a short TCO sheet and include unit economics per 1M tokens.
[00:12:22]
[00:13:00]
[00:13:30] [Speaker 2]: (crosstalk) — I see a question about concurrency limits on Hosted?
[00:13:36] Jordan: Hosted has soft concurrency limits; we can provision higher caps for pilots but Dedicated gives strict throughput guarantees.
[00:13:45]
[00:14:10] Priya: Ok. Anything else on pipeline?
[00:14:14] Alex: Just that we'll push Zenith as highest priority — exec intro in the next week would be ideal.
[00:14:22] Maya: We'll aim for that.
[00:14:30]
[00:15:00] Maya: Quick recap and owners: Maya to share joint deck, TCO sheet; Jordan to schedule benchmarks and SOC 2 matrix; Carlos to share legal playbook; Alex to arrange exec intros and dataset handoffs; all agree?
[00:15:12] Alex: Yep.
[00:15:15] Priya: Agreed.
[00:15:18] Tom: Agreed.
[00:15:22]
[00:15:30] Maya: Ok we'll follow up in a shared folder. Thanks everyone.
[00:15:36] [00:15:36] End of recording (note: some segments clipped due to mobile audio).
